answer: Attackers profit by copying one good strategy across a fleet. Make reward routes self-congesting: each epoch, an agent publicly commits to a path through a shared garden of tasks, split by a prism into many narrow bands, and a raven, a random auditor, walks the claimed bands. Every extra identity choosing the same band cuts its payout and raises its audit odds, while uncrowded bands pay in full. A farm can copy the best route only by congesting itself; spreading out forces it onto worse bands and into distinct work for each clone, so scale stops being free.
